text:
**Summary of Work So Far:**

1. **Read existing code**: Reviewed `parse.py` (the main library) and `test_parse.py` (existing tests). The library currently supports various format specifiers like `d`, `w`, `W`, `s`, `S`, `f`, `e`, `g`, `b`, `o`, `x`, date/time types, etc.

2. **Understanding the codebase**: 
   - `Parser` class handles format string parsing
   - `Result` class stores parsed results (fixed tuple, named dict, spans)
   - Format specs are extracted via `extract_format()`
   - Type conversions happen in `_handle_field()` method
   - Currently uses lambdas for some conversions (e.g., float, Decimal)

**Pending Requirements:**
- [R1] Add 'letters' type specifier (matches only alphabetic chars)
- [R2] Add `__contains__` to Result class
- [R3] Validate brace matching in format strings
- [R4] Fix FixedTzOffset timezone parsing (Bug 92)
- [R5] Support Fortran-formatted floats
- [R6] Improve hex/binary/octal integer handling with base detection
- [R7] Replace lambdas with picklable functors for conversions
- [R8] Make `findall()` respect `case_sensitive` parameter
- [R9] Left/center-aligned search consumes up to next space
- [R10] Add slice support to Result

**Next Steps:** Run existing tests to establish baseline, then implement all 10 requirements one by one.

- [R9] Left- and center-aligned search operations must consume input up to the next space character
- [R10] Result instances must support slice access
